newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's peseta ends firmer on mark.
newsitem.headline: Spain's peseta ends firmer on mark.

text.p: The peseta overcame earlier weakness to firm against the mark in late trade on Thursday, traders said.
A lira in a better shape contributed to support for the Spanish unit, undermined in the last few days by EMU worries.

"The peseta made a good use of the dollar's and lira's recovery...we had already noticed this morning less tension in the market because short term money market interest rates were more stable," a forex dealer in Madrid said.
By 1605 GMT, near the end of the session, the peseta was trading at 84.67/69 per mark which compares to an opening level at 84.75/78 and Wednesday's close at 84.80/83.
Dealers said the recovery was also due to profit taking after several days of general weakness in peripheral currencies.
During the past few days, Spain's unit was put under pressure and it reached 84.85 against the mark. The Bank of Spain was also reported to have been buying pesetas.
"In the market there is also the fear of the central bank's intervention. Although today there is no need of it," a dealer added.
